correctness.rationale: The conditional one-contact recursion follows directly from the acyclic tree and includes attempted contact with the already infected parent with probability 1/degree. The complete unlabelled-tree generator inductively attaches each possible leaf and uses a tree-center rooted AHU canonical invariant. Exact Fraction computations exhaust all 2..13 vertex trees (1301 classes at order 13) and find leaf maximum equality. Exact 14-vertex witness scores were independently reproduced by direct path-prefix probability summation; 49/16−1763/576=1/576 and vertex 0 uniquely maximizes.

originality.rationale: Compared the exact claimed tree-seed order cutoff and the equivalent first-repeat walk against open primary texts (Kenah–Robins, Gómez et al., Tishby–Biham–Katzav, Enright–Kao) and mathematical research records. The strongest same-process paper gives ensemble-averaged first-repeat lengths on Erdős–Rényi graphs and does not imply a deterministic fixed-tree vertex-optimality threshold. No direct or stronger covering statement was found in inspected materials. Residual discovery risk is recorded.
residual_risks: An unindexed result in first-repeat random walk or epidemic source-centrality literature could imply this small-tree boundary.
The numerical margin is small, though certified exactly; no claim of practical effect size.
No independent mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The naturally motivated seed-selection question asks whether peripheral seeds can always maximize a constrained-contact epidemic on trees. The result locates the first qualitative failure exactly at order 14 and gives a sharply certified explicit exception. This is a meaningful structural boundary about topology and source choice, not a small numerical improvement presented as epidemiological magnitude; complete smaller-order classification and an exact witness are essential to the conclusion.
